note: Verifies what a DuckDB quack client-server session (v1.5.3 + quack core extension) actually supports over loopback: auth handshake, the remote DML/DDL surface, transaction propagation, concurrent append, and failure signalling. No statistical distribution applies: each row is a pass/fail or exact-error observation, not a timing sample. Section 5 latency is machine-dependent context, not evidence.
subject: DuckDB v1.5.3 (Variegata) + quack core extension
topology: single Windows machine, loopback; client and server are both DuckDB

1_basic_roundtrip.claim: After ATTACH, the client reads remote tables transparently.

2_auth.result: Invalid Input Error: Authentication failed -> remote schema not created
Invalid Input Error: Could not find a Quack authentication token

3_remote_write_surface.note: Key finding the README does not spell out: the 'multiplayer' story is append + DDL, not arbitrary mutation, in direct SQL.
fail: Binder Error: Can only update base table
3_remote_write_surface.DELETE FROM remote.t: fail: Binder Error: Can only delete from base table
3_remote_write_surface.PRAGMA database_list (remote): fail: Not implemented Error: InMemory not implemented yet (table reads still work)

3b_update_delete_serverside_workaround.claim: UPDATE/DELETE are not impossible, only the direct 'UPDATE remote.table' grammar is un-wired; pushing the SQL string to the server works.
3b_update_delete_serverside_workaround.direct UPDATE remote.upd_probe: fail: Binder Error: Can only update base table

3c_transaction_rollback_not_propagated.claim: A remote multi-statement transaction's ROLLBACK is not propagated: the inserted row survives.
3c_transaction_rollback_not_propagated.sql: BEGIN; INSERT INTO remote.tx_probe VALUES (1); ROLLBACK;
3c_transaction_rollback_not_propagated.result: fail (row remained despite ROLLBACK) — contradicts docs' 'transactions are forwarded'
3c_transaction_rollback_not_propagated.implication: Do not rely on remote BEGIN/ROLLBACK for business integrity in beta.

4_concurrent_writers.claim: Two separate processes appending concurrently both commit with no row loss or lockout.

5_latency_context_only.note: Localhost round-trip cost, machine-dependent CONTEXT, not an evidence claim. Shows the boundary tax vs in-process zero-copy.
5_latency_context_only.honest_reading: The official '~3.5x faster than Arrow Flight' claim is vs another wire protocol. The absolute cost of leaving in-process zero-copy is real (0ms -> 0.5-1s). Arrow Flight direct comparison is out of scope (not measured).

6_server_failure.claim: Killing the server surfaces a connect error immediately, not a silent hang.
6_server_failure.observed: IO Error: Failed to send message: IO Error: Could not connect to server error for HTTP POST to 'http://localhost:9494/quack'

cited_not_measured.claim: quack is ~3.5x faster than Arrow Flight.
cited_not_measured.source: official quack materials; a different-wire-protocol comparison. No Arrow Flight baseline was executed in this run.
project roadmap at time of writing; v1.5.3 is beta. Cited, not verified by this run.

non_findings_honesty.note: An early file-backed ATTACH failed with 'Catalog remote does not exist', but a clean retry (after clearing the stale port) attached fine (t_rows=0). This was a port-race test artifact, not a quack file-vs-memory limit, so it is NOT reported as a limitation.
